summary: Recalculates a strided array of particle orientation axes. Reads a source direction (and a Y component) from an object reached through VirtualDispatchHelper(&dword_5EA510) at offset +36, scales the X and Z components by -0.03125, then walks entries of 10 floats starting at unk_8AC840 up to the end marker flt_8ACAC0. For each entry it derives the three axis vectors from the direction and the previous row, computes their cross product, and normalizes it to length this[4]/2 (or applies a default axis of length this[4]/2 along X when the magnitude is zero). Called by sub_4CC970 and ParticleEffectPhysics.

operations.description: Call VirtualDispatchHelper(&dword_5EA510) and take a pointer at result+36 to obtain the source direction data v2.
Compute scaled direction components: v3 = v2[0] * -0.03125 (X), v13 = v2[1] (Y kept raw), v4 = v2[2] * -0.03125 (Z).
Iterate over the strided entry array with an entry stride of 10 floats, starting at unk_8AC840 and continuing while the entry address is below flt_8ACAC0.
Per entry, write the derived direction vector: X = v3, Y = (previous Y - v13) * 0.03125, Z = v4 into the entry slots.
Compute the cross product of the two direction vectors: v14, v15, and v16 = v7 - v9 from the raw component products.
Store the cross product as the entry's axis vectors: *(v5-1) = v14, *v5 = v15, v5[1] = v16.
Per entry, check the squared magnitude of the axis vector; when it is > 0.0 the vector is normalized.
Normalize the axis: scale each component by this[4] * 0.5 / sqrt(magnitude) so the vector length becomes this[4]/2.
When the magnitude is zero, set a default axis: X = this[4] * 0.5, Y = 0, Z = 0.
Advance the entry pointer by the 10-float stride and continue while below flt_8ACAC0.

unresolved: The object type behind VirtualDispatchHelper(&dword_5EA510) and the meaning of its +36 field are unknown.
The 10-float entry layout and the exact meaning of each axis row in the unk_8AC840 array are inferred from the arithmetic only.
flt_8ACAC0 is treated as an end-marker address for the strided array; its identity as an array terminator is DERIVED.
